scope: R159 read-only analysis of the FA910A launch plan (no machine use, no code change)
confirmed_launch_plan: [FA910A] plan input_N=41792 kernel_N=43776 key_limit=41769 original_pad=23 ; core_budget=30 blockDim=30 B=1 H=7 N=43776 D=128 Br=128 Bc=304
plan_source: historical log evidence in the repository receipts, not a new run

retraction.claim_i_was_about_to_make: the FA kernel is forced to 64x64 tiles because pick_tile requires exact divisibility and 41792 = 64 x 653 with 653 prime
retraction.why_it_is_wrong: _kernel_sequence_length pads the sequence to kernel_N=43776 = 18 x lcm(128,304) whenever the unpadded shape would produce tiles smaller than 128x128, so the kernel actually runs Br=128 Bc=304 on the padded length
retraction.status: retracted before being proposed as a candidate

padding_arithmetic.note: attention is quadratic so the wasted work grows with the square of the padded length

candidate_identified.what: launch the same CANN flash_attention kernel on N=41792 with Br=128 Bc=304 instead of padding to 43776
candidate_identified.why_it_should_be_numerically_identical: the padded keys are zeroed and excluded by key_limit, and the padded query rows produce outputs that are discarded, so dropping them removes no real contribution; row blocks are independent in flash attention, so per-row accumulation order over the 304-wide key blocks is unchanged
candidate_identified.expected_saving_basis: 8.4 percent fewer tiles at the same tile shape, applied to a 7.607 s kernel term
candidate_identified.what_it_needs: a one-line condition change in _kernel_sequence_length, then a bitwise comparison of the two paths in the same process, exactly like the R148 pattern where the native result is still returned
candidate_identified.risk: medium: it exercises the kernel tail-block path that the padding currently avoids, so both correctness and speed must be measured
candidate_identified.authorization_required: yes, because it changes the attention path even though the expectation is bit-identical

what_this_does_not_do: it does not close the gap between 41 TFLOPs and the roughly 69 TFLOPs the 10 s path needs
it does not touch the softmax or the cube efficiency of the CANN kernel
conclusion: the FA plan is already well tuned on the axes I could inspect (Br=128, Bc=304, 30 cores, documented repartitioning win). The only clearly wasteful, quantified and likely-free item is the 9.7 percent padding overhead, worth about 0.74 s per step. Reaching 10 s still needs the kernel to get materially faster, which is new kernel work and needs the user decision.
